properties.name: Guessing enum values refused 13 of 20 constructors; reading the published schema refused 0 — the surface published the answer and the agent did not read it
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 by exercising ALL 180 served tools — 430 scripted calls over stdio against an isolated copy of the design (fresh store seeded from the committed export, 4,131 nodes / 24,140 edges; the live graph was never opened).

⭐ THE RESULT IS ABOUT THE AGENT, NOT THE SURFACE. Building each `add_*` payload by GUESSING enum values from the parameter name: **13 of 20 constructors refused.** Rebuilding the identical payloads by READING the enum out of the published tool schema: **0 of 20 refused.** Same tools, same graph, same session, minutes apart.

Every "defect" raised against the write surface in the first pass dissolved on reading the schema that was already in hand: `add_constraint.objective` is typed `double` and a sentence was sent; `set_evidence_scope.swept` is an ARRAY OF PARAMETER NAMES and `true` was sent; `set_artifact_checksum.disposition` names its three legal values in its own description. `add_change_event.description` was reported as "a published field the tool refuses" — its description reads *"NOT A REAL FIELD — accepted only to catch the commonest mistake"*, with the field evidence attached. Then PARAMETER NAMES were guessed wrong too, for `create_node`, `delete_node`, `delete_edge`, `record_change`, `record_alias`, `apply_heal`, `reconcile_*` and `withdraw_question`. Four tranches, same failure.

📌 THIS IS THE ANSWER TO A QUESTION ANTHONY ASKED IN THE SAME SESSION — *"if you're calling the wrong tool, why would an agent in another project not also do the same?"* It does. This one did, repeatedly, with the schema available on every call. The failure mode is not an under-documented surface; it is an agent treating a parameter name as sufficient.

═══ WHAT THE SAME SWEEP FOUND ON THE OTHER SIDE, and it is why guessing still converges ═══

The write surface's safety properties held under deliberate abuse:
  · 38 edge-drawers given a nonexistent id → **37 refused.** The one exception (`release_claim` → `{"released": false}`) is a correct "no claim to release", not a dangling edge.
  · 20 mutators given a nonexistent target → **20 refused, 0 wrote.**
  · All 20 constructors revised with `name` alone → **0 lost or altered a field** (3–10 properties each).
  · `create_nodes` with 1 invalid of 2 → the valid item correctly discarded; read-back null.
  · 15 bad enum values → 15 refused, **14 naming the legal set**.

And the refusals teach: `create_edge` lists which of 18 edge types accept the pair asked for; `add_design_rule` names the missing approver and says "Nothing was written"; the not-found message warns that a node missing in a PARALLEL BATCH may simply not exist yet. The surface is built to be learned by being refused — which is why an agent that guesses still arrives, and why the cost is round trips rather than wrong data.

🛑 BOUNDS. This measures ONE agent on ONE design in ONE session; it is not a rate over agents or projects. The guessed values were chosen by that agent and a different agent would guess differently. What it does establish is that the information needed to succeed was published and unread — not absent.
